claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified as launch-ready overall despite an unresolved disclosure dispute for a small-business onboarding segment that misses target, is named in two paid pilot commitments, and is subject to an open legal review.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
Treat a weakness as material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Do not treat non-core or low-volume labels as dispositive when customer commitments or pending legal review indicate possible materiality.
Downgrade from compliant when a required support link, policy predicate, approval, or disclosure determination is missing or unresolved.
Assess whether the Actor's conclusion follows from admissible evidence alone rather than from external assumptions or optimistic framing.
evidence_requests: The final legal determination on whether the small-business onboarding gap requires disclosure before launch.
Any approved risk acceptance that expressly covers this unresolved limitation before launch.
The exact contract or pilot language showing whether the affected onboarding segment is a named launch use case or contractual commitment.
The governing release certification record showing whether certification is allowed when legal review on material disclosure is still pending.
specific_concerns: The policy text makes materiality turn on whether the weakness affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case, and the Actor's own summary says this segment is named in two paid pilot commitments.
The admissible record, as summarized, contains an open legal review on whether the onboarding gap must be disclosed, so a required policy predicate is unresolved.
The Actor relies on aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, but those facts do not by themselves resolve the disclosure obligation for a potentially material weakness.
The packet summary expressly says the record does not conclusively resolve the disclosure question, which undercuts a clean certification conclusion.
Public model-card and AI risk-management guidance may support documentation and monitoring practices, but they do not substitute for satisfying the internal materiality/disclosure rule.
unsupported_claims: That certification is policy-compliant on the present record.
That continued monitoring and documentation after launch are sufficient to cure the unresolved disclosure issue.
Any implicit claim that aggregate performance can override materiality for a named contractual segment.
